title: Do not sell options when implied volatility is below realized
summary: The speaker reviews a social media trade: sell an NVIDIA put spread, short $210, long $207.50, stock near $224, 8 days to expiry, for about $0.30 ($30) with $220 max loss. The trade hit max loss. He would have refused it: a poor entry and implied volatility trading below realized since late May, so the seller was not paid for the risk.

params.label: Implied minus realized
params.help: Average gap between implied and realized volatility, in vol points.

steps.caption: NVIDIA near $224. A put spread is sold at $210/$207.50 for $0.30 with 8 days left.
Realized volatility: how much NVIDIA actually moved.
Implied volatility had been below realized since about the third week of May.
A negative gap means the seller is paid less than the risk taken. $30 credit against $220 max loss.
Rule: when implied is at or below realized, do not sell options.

takeaways: Compare implied with realized volatility before selling options.
When implied is at or below realized, you are not paid enough for the risk.
The cited trade risked $220 to make $30 and hit max loss.
caveats: VAY is the speaker's proprietary score; it is promotional and unverified.
Trade figures are quoted from the video and not checked here.
